title: AV truck fleets win 5-Year exemption on warning beacons
key_facts: The Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration granted a five-year exemption on Wednesday 7 Oct 2026, running through 7 Oct 2031.
It lets Level 4 autonomous trucks use cab-mounted amber warning beacons instead of reflective triangles; it covers Aurora and any other Level 4 carrier that notifies the agency first.
It replaces four three-month waivers Aurora has used since October 2025; Kodiak AI, Waabi and Stack AV opted in.
Under the waiver Aurora ran beacons on 34 trucks over more than 500,000 miles, with beacons active for nearly 10 hours and no faults reported.
Beacons must activate within five minutes of a stop; trucks must stay inside validated operating zones and may not haul hazardous materials or passengers.
Opponents included OOIDA, the Truck Safety Coalition and Advocates for Highway and Auto Safety; supporters included the American Trucking Associations, Waymo, Kodiak, Volvo and Amazon.
FMCSA said it lacks data showing triangles significantly improve driver reaction time; it had denied a similar Aurora and Waymo request in December 2024.
quote_evidence: The exemption runs through Oct. 7, 2031, and covers Aurora Operations plus any other Level 4 carrier that notifies the agency first, under a notice signed by Administrator Derek Barrs.
It replaces four three-month waivers Aurora has operated under since October 2025.
It said it lacks data showing triangles significantly improve driver reaction time, and that whether such devices improve traffic safety at all is a historically unresolved question.
why_it_matters_hint: Removes a rule that required a person to walk out and place triangles behind a stopped truck.
notes: Older news re-dated: the exemption was granted on 7 Oct; FreightWaves reported it on 8 Oct.
